findings.finding: The bear path turns a temporary digestion into a permanent 20-year stall, and the table's bear condition line does not describe the number shown. The bear growth_anchor (-5% FY2028, own_history tier) is justified as the largest customer cutting purchases 'for several quarters, as in Credo's own FY2024 (+4.8% after +73%)'; Credo's own FY2024 was followed by +126%/+206%. The engine's growth-fade rule (a lever on the gaps row, no company data) then carries the -5% into revenue of 2.40B -> 2.34B -> 2.34B -> 2.37B -> 2.42B -> 2.48B (FY2028-FY2033) and about 1-4% a year to FY2047, at a flat 22% margin. Combined with bear ROIC 10% < cost of equity 11% this gives a forward P/E of 9.5-9.6x and the -85% bear (24.3$ today, 21.7-24.3$ years 1-5). The shown bear is a structural break (permanent loss of the AI interconnect franchise), not the cited temporary event, which breaks the rule to test temporary against structural explanations and makes the headline downside unsupported by its own evidence.
findings.where: inputs.json forecast.overrides[0] (growth_anchor bear) + engine growth fade; casefile company_path.fiscal_years.bear and scenarios.bear; table_he.md bear column and bear condition line
findings.fix: Either (a) model the evidenced temporary case: one or two digestion years and then a recovery path tied to Credo's own post-FY2024 recovery and the >600M optical / 1.6T evidence, or (b) keep a structural bear but state it as such in the condition line and back it with structural evidence (share loss to MaxLinear/Astera/optics at named sockets), with growth beyond FY2029 supplied as an explicit, evidenced override rather than the engine fade of a negative anchor. Rerun ticker-value; review_counter to confirm.

findings.finding: Bear ROIC 10% is a hypothesis tagged own_history. The reason ('if competition at 1.6T and digestion continue, ROIC on new capital falls to about 10%, near the cost of capital') derives no 10% from any Credo number: the cited items show 26% pre-tax post-acquisition and 72% pre-acquisition. The bear multiple (justification 'peak') rests on it.
findings.fix: Derive the bear ROIC from Credo's own record (e.g. FY2024 digestion-year ROIC from pf_history_companyfacts, or post-DustPhotonics after-tax ROIC under the bear margin of 22%) or relabel it as a hypothesis with no evidence id, and show the sensitivity of the bear value to it.

findings.finding: Bull ROIC 40% is not what its reason says. The text calls it 'midway between 26% after the acquisition and 72% before' (both PRE-tax); the midpoint is 49% pre-tax, about 41-42% after tax at the ~15% rate used for the base (26% pre-tax -> 22% after tax). Pre-tax and after-tax bases are mixed across scenarios, and the bull's 96x year-0 / 64x year-1 forward P/E depends on this number.
findings.where: inputs.json company_path.scenarios.bull.reason_he / roic 0.4 versus scenarios.base (0.22 after tax)
findings.fix: State every scenario's ROIC on one basis (after tax, as the economics formula uses), recompute the bull value from the stated derivation, and correct the Hebrew reason.

findings.finding: A peak multiple is paid without a comparison to named competitors. Bull year-0 forward P/E 96.4x and year-1 64.4x (bull year-1 price 638$, +281%) are labelled 'unproven' but still shown, and there is no compare to Astera Labs, Marvell or Broadcom at a comparable stage: every competitor entry has forward_pe_and_growth = 'gap: FMP quote denied'. The IB connector (read-only get_price_snapshot) was available for competitor prices, and their EPS is in the saved filings, so the gap could have been closed. Own history is trailing GAAP P/E only (51.6-424.3, 'tiny-earnings effect'), so it does not test a forward multiple either.
findings.fix: Retrieve ALAB and MRVL (and AVGO) prices read-only from IB with their attributed or reported EPS to get a dated forward/trailing P/E, compare to the bull and base multiple paths, and flag the bull as paying a peak multiple when it exceeds the closest-stage competitor (ALAB); keep the bull a separately sized, explicitly hypothetical case.

findings.finding: The FY2027 current-year revenue is tiered 'guidance' but rests on a third-party transcript excerpt (ex_tr_20260901, retrieval search_excerpt, not restated in the written release). The 'more than 85%' floor is then raised with the mean guide-beat ratio 1.105, although that mean is driven by early small-base quarters (+12.5% to +19.7%) and the last two beats were +1.6% and +1.9%; the guidance_track list also holds each of the 7 quarters twice under two labels.
findings.fix: Confirm the FY2027 statement from a primary source (issuer webcast/IR transcript) or downgrade the tier to attributed; use the recent-quarters beat ratio (or none: the floor plus the Q2 guide) and show the difference (~+56M); deduplicate guidance_track so the n and mean are on 7 unique quarters.

findings.finding: The dominant base lever, growth after FY2028, is on an engine rule: the base revenue path 3.59B -> 4.77B -> 6.02B -> 7.29B -> 8.57B -> 9.76B (FY2028-FY2033) comes from the generic fade, with no company guidance or evidenced driver beyond FY2028. The gaps row lists 'growth fade pace' among eight engine-rule levers, and the base-rate warning (about 2% of companies of this size sustained ~23% real growth for ten years) is shown correctly as a warning only, but the table does not say that this one lever carries most of the base fair value of 162$.
findings.where: table_he.md rows 'הנחות בלי נתון של החברה' and 'כמה התחזית אופטימית'; casefile company_path.fiscal_years.base
findings.fix: Keep the gaps row and the warning, and add one plain sentence (or a sensitivity line behind the scenes) stating how much of the base value depends on post-FY2028 growth; where possible tie FY2029-FY2031 to company evidence (1.6T ramp, SiPho design wins, capacity deposits of 88M + 102.4M as a capacity ceiling).

findings.finding: The Bull 1.6T AEC share retention and the bull 9-10%-a-quarter pace through FY2028 are hypotheses; the condition line marks the first one, and the pace extends two quarters of data (Q1 actual, Q2 guide) over six more quarters.
findings.fix: Mark the pace as an extrapolation in the bull condition line as well.

findings.finding: Tooling: pack-merge will overwrite the two value-stage PACK fixes (identity evidence ids, cash_cost_ratio padded from 17 to 22 values) on any rerun, so a repair pass that reruns ticker-value from pack-merge can silently revert them.
findings.fix: Have repair reapply both fixes in the position files (analyst parts) rather than only in the merged pack, and confirm cash_cost_ratio has 22 values per scenario after any rerun.
